subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.

spec.name: Hydra of the Deep Fen
spec.description: A five-headed hydra in a God of War-style finish: a coiled plated serpent trunk rising to a shoulder crown where five bone-crested necks fan out around one dominant central head, all dark slate scales, weathered bone armour and a toxic green glow burning in eyes, throats and scale seams.
spec.layout: Front (+Z): five heads fan around a tall dominant central head; the two inner heads at x ±1.85 y ~4.7, the two outer heads lower and wider at x ±2.75 y ~4.15, the central head tallest at y ~5.0, all snouts pointing up-and-forward (+Z) so every face reads from the front. Below them the shoulder crown at [0, 3.0, 0.9] sits on a massive rearing trunk: a thick coil lying on the floor at the rear (z -1.2..0.4), then the trunk rising forward to a deep chest with a bone gorget and a broad shoulder hump. Two stocky digitigrade forelegs under the chest plant clawed three-toed feet on the floor; the heavy tail sweeps back from [0, 0.85, -1.2] down to the floor, tapering to a spiked tip at z ~-3.4. Style on every part: dark desaturated slate-teal scales with pale bone plating on brows, gorget, dorsal spikes and claws; hard faceted low-poly surfaces; ink-dark seam lines; glowing toxic green only in eyes, throat gullets, tongue and the crack seams between chest plates — the glow marks the monster's rage, everything else stays cold stone and bone.

parts.builds: The rearing serpent trunk and shoulder crown. Build a loft or sweep along the spine path from a broad coil on the floor at the rear (radius ~0.85 flattened under by shift so it rests on y=0) rising forward through the chest (radius ~0.7 at spine2) to the shoulder hump at the neckCrown mount (radius ~0.6, spine3), skinning over spine1..3. Back and flanks wear scaleDark to scaleMid fading to scaleTeal on the upper flanks and scaleLight on ridge tops; the underside is pale belly. Details: a gorget of overlapping bone plates across the chest front (bone with boneShade under-plates and ink gaps); broad transverse belly scutes (belly, inked seams) from the coil up the throat line; a dorsal ridge of faceted bone spikes (bone) running spine1 to spine3, each a frustum or extruded blade seated on the surface with a glow scale-crack part (glow) seated in the seam beside every third spike; a few scattered raised scale plates (scaleTeal, small extruded hexagons) on the shoulders; two ink eye-like glow slits are NOT part of this part (heads own eyes). The top of this part ends cleanly at the neckCrown mount where all five necks root.
parts.attaches: Rises from the floor coil; spine3 ends at mount neckCrown where the necks part roots all five necks; spine1 hands off at mount tailRoot to the tail part; hipL/hipR mounts on the lower flank are shared with the legs part.

parts.builds: The heavy serpent tail. A sweep from mount tailRoot (radius ~0.5) curving back and down through tail1..tail4, tapering to ~0.06 at the tip which rests and curls slightly on the floor at z ~-3.4. Colours: scaleDark on top blending to scaleTeal at the sides, belly underneath, gradient to scaleLight near the tip. Details: a continuous row of alternating bone spikes (bone, small frustums) down the dorsal line via b.along on the tail sweep; three bony tail rings (boneShade bands swept at t ~0.3/0.55/0.75, ink-edged); a barbed tip of two crossed bone blades (extruded, bone with boneShade edges) at the very end; a few scale-teal plates stuck along the flanks.
parts.attaches: Roots at mount tailRoot on spine1's rear; everything else of the part is free-hanging to the floor.

parts.builds: Two stocky digitigrade forelegs. For each side build the chain hipX-kneeX-ankleX-footX as a lofted limb: massive thigh (radius ~0.32) with a heavy shoulder mass blending into the torso flank at mount hipX, knee bent back, ankle forward, and a broad three-toed foot planted flat on the floor (foot joint at y 0.12, toes splayed forward +Z with the middle toe longest). Colours: scaleDark upper leg, scaleTeal shin, belly-toned inner thigh. Details per foot: three clawed toes built as tapered bone frustums (bone) each tipped with a dark ink claw point, plus a rear dewclaw; bone shin guards (extruded plates, bone over boneShade) strapped over the knee with ink bands; a spike cluster (bone) on each knee and elbow; a few scale plates (scaleTeal) stuck on the thigh. Feet rest exactly on y=0.
parts.attaches: Thigh tops merge into the torso flanks at mounts hipL and hipR on spine2; feet plant on the floor between the tail root and the body coil.

parts.builds: All five serpentine necks rising from the shoulder crown. For each neck build its chain (neckXX1..3) as a sweep, radius ~0.26 at the crown tapering to ~0.14 where it meets its head mount, the outer necks thicker (~0.3 to 0.18) and the central neck the thickest (~0.3 to 0.16). Colour each neck: scaleDark along the top (nape), scaleTeal on the sides, pale belly strip on the underside facing inward-down. Details per neck: a double row of faceted bone spikes down the nape placed with b.along along the sweep (largest at the base, shrinking to the head, bone with boneShade bases); 3-4 ink seam rings low on each neck; a glowing throat gullet: a strip of glow-coloured scale-like segments (glow, tiny extruded plates) running up the front of the underside from crown to jaw line on every neck, brightest on the central neck; scattered raised scale plates (scaleLight) on the outer curve. The five necks must visually braid apart from the crown: slight overlap at the base is fine, separation by neck2.
parts.attaches: All five necks root at mount neckCrown on spine3, positioned at the crown's five root points; each neck tip ends exactly at its head mount (headC, headIL, headIR, headOL, headOR) where the heads part begins.

parts.builds: All five heads, one per head mount, identical construction with the central head 15% larger and all jaws slightly agape showing teeth. Each head rides its headX joint and is aimed along that joint's dir. Build: an angular faceted skull (loft or frustum boxes: narrow snout widening to the jaw hinge), a heavy bone brow ridge (extruded bone plate over each eye, boneShade underside), two swept-back horns (spikes or swept beziers, bone with ink tips) per head, jaw hinge cheeks of scaleMid, a lower jaw as a separate piece on the jawX joint with a gum-dark interior (gum) and two rows of triangular teeth (tooth, small cones) on both upper and lower jaws, a tongue (tongue colour, flat extruded blade) lolling from the central jaw only, and a pair of big glowing eyes (glow kit on small sphere or extruded almond parts, glow with a glowCore highlight dot, ink socket rim) set under the brow. Behind each jaw hinge a short neck-frill of membrane-coloured webbed spikes (b.membrane or thin extruded blades, membrane with bone spines). Add ink nostril slits on the snout top and 2-3 bone plating shards down the skull midline. The central head additionally gets a crown of three small bone horns and a brighter throat glow.
parts.attaches: Each head seats onto its neck at the head mounts headC, headIL, headIR, headOL, headOR, riding headC/jawC, headIL/jawIL, headIR/jawIR, headOL/jawOL, headOR/jawOR.

I need to write a spec for a five-headed hydra, God of War style (dark, aggressive, scaled monster with glow accents). Let me design it.

Model space: +Y up, faces +Z, left +X, centered on x=0, standing on y=0.

Hydra: massive serpentine body rearing up, with a long thick neck splitting into five necks/heads. God of War style: dark desaturated scales, bone plating, glowing green/teal eyes and throat, sharp spines, claws.

Plan the anatomy:
- Body: thick serpentine trunk from a coiled base on the ground, rearing up. Body length along z, maybe the tail extends back (-Z), chest rears up toward +Z.
- Five necks rising from a shoulder fan at the top of the body, spread out; each neck has a head with jaw (upper/lower), horns, glowing eyes.
- Legs: hydra in GoW style — could have two stocky forelegs and a tail. Let's include two muscular forelegs with claws planted on ground, and a heavy tail coiling behind.

Size: something like width 4.5 (spread necks), height 5.2, length 6.5.

Layout decision: root body rising from y=0 at rear, sweeping forward and up; chest/shoulder mass at about z=+0.5, y=2.6. Five necks radiate from the shoulder crown: center neck tall (apex ~5.2), two mid necks at ±1.3 x, two outer necks at ±2.2 x, heads spread. Tail sweeps back and down to the ground at -Z, resting on floor. Two forelegs from lower chest down to ground.

Mounts: neckRoot (shoulder crown center), tailRoot, legMountL/R (or shoulder joints per leg), maybe headBase per neck — but necks built by one builder probably. Let's split parts:

1. body — trunk/torso, serpentine coils at base, chest, plates, spikes, belly. Rides spine joints.
2. necks — all five necks as chains from neckRoot mount, sweeps, spines along each.
3. heads — five heads with jaws, horns, eyes, teeth. Hmm, heads need to attach to neck tips — that's fine, mounts define neck tip positions. But heads builder needs the neck tip joints. Could combine necks+heads into one part (big). Alternatively:
   - part1: body (trunk, tail? no tail separate)
   - part2: legs (two forelegs + claws)
   - part3: tail
   - part4: necks (5 chains + sweeps + dorsal spines)
   - part5: heads (five heads w/ jaws, eyes, horns, teeth) — attaches to neck tips via head joints listed in joints spec.

That's 5 parts, each reasonably even. Budget: body 200, legs 140, tail 120, necks 180, heads 260. Total 900.

Joints skeleton (created in order, parents first):
- root: "body" spine joint at [0, 1.2, 0.2], dir up-forward? Let's make spine chain: body (root) at base [0, 0.9, -0.4], then chest at [0, 2.0, 0.6], shoulderCrown at [0, 3.0, 0.9]. Actually chains: the spec lists joints individually. Let me define:

- "spine2" parent spine1 at [0, 1.8, 0.2] dir [0, 0.7, 1] role spine

Necks: five chains each with 3 joints + head joint. That's a lot of joints to list. Each neck: n1..n3 + head joint + jaw joint (child of head). 5 necks × (3+1+1) = 25 joints. Plus legs: legL hip, knee, ankle, foot = 4 × 2 = 8. Tail: 4 joints. Spine 3. Total ~40 joints. Fine but the joints array is long; that's acceptable. But maybe simplify: necks as chains with names listed; the joints spec must enumerate since each part lists joints its geometry rides. I can specify compactly but must be explicit. Let me define naming: neckA1..3, neckB..., or neckC (center), neckL1/L2 (inner left, outer left), neckR1/R2.

Heads: headC, headL1, headL2, headR1, headR2, each with jaw joint jawC etc.

Legs: hipL, kneeL, ankleL, footL (role leg), same R. Tail: tail1..4 role tail.

Actually necks maybe 3 joints each is enough (long serpentine necks ~2m each). Let each neck chain: base at shoulder crown region, rising.

- Center: base [0, 3.05, 0.95] → [0, 3.9, 1.2] → [0, 4.6, 1.3], head at [0, 5.0, 1.35]. Height ~5.2 total with head.

Width: heads spread to ±3.2 with snouts? Outer heads at x ±2.6 plus head length ~0.9 → size x ~6? Maybe tighten: outer heads at ±2.3, snout forward. Width ~5.4.

Height: center head top ~5.3.

Length: tail extends to z=-3.5, snouts to z=+2.2. Body base coil near z -1..1. Length ~6.

Let me set size: [5.6, 5.4, 6.4].

Inner L: neckL1A... naming: neckLA1? Use names: neckL1, neckL2, neckL3 for inner-left; neckLO1.. for outer? Better: neckIL1..3 (inner left), neckOL1..3 (outer left), same R. Heads: headIL, headOL, headC. Jaws: jawIL etc.

I'm working out leg geometry using the joint positions for hip, knee, ankle, and foot, planning to build each leg segment with capsule shapes along those points for a safe, compact construction.

Sketching toe and foot pad shapes so nothing dips below the floor, then mirroring the whole leg between left and right sides, and adding detail touches like hip spheres, knee spikes, and thin ink-band rods along the shin for texture.

Working out toe and claw positions so the middle toe extends furthest with claws adding a bit more length, keeping the foot proportions tidy. Then I'm planning spike clusters at the knee and elbow, positioning them outward and forward with directional vectors pulled from the palette.

I'm planning out the tail joint positions, placing them progressively lower and further back so the tail curves down toward the floor with a tapered tip.

I'm using a sweep path with the four tail joints as bones, defining a radius taper from thick at the base to thin at the tip, plus color sectors for belly, sides, and scales with banded shading toward the tip.

For the rings, I'm layering slightly larger offset sweeps at each segment boundary for bone shading plus thin ink outlines on either side. Then I'm placing tapering dorsal spikes along the tail sweep using an alternating offset pattern that shrinks toward the tip.

Still writing spike placement logic...

Now I'm adding small hexagonal flank plates as scaled cylinders at symmetric flank angles, and starting on crossed leaf-blade shapes for the tail tip.

I need to clamp the blade's vertical extent to stay within height bounds, tightening it to roughly ±0.1 and adjusting the tip tangent slightly downward near the path's end. Then I'll write the tail path using Catmull-Rom interpolation with colors from the palette, pulling in THREE and the rng helper for subtle spike jitter.

I'm figuring out how to type the buildTorso function's context parameter safely, considering whether to loosely type it to avoid conflicting with an existing Ctx declaration.

Now I'm planning the torso geometry itself: placing spine joints, then sketching out a series of loft stations rising from the floor to the crown, adjusting widths and heights at each station so the trunk tapers naturally and the top closes out at the correct height.

For surface detail, I'm figuring out how to add spikes along the dorsal ridge by casting rays downward onto the trunk's surface mesh at intervals along its length, so I can position cone shapes precisely where they hit.

I'll make the spikes using tapered cone geometry that decreases in size toward the tail, spacing roughly fourteen of them, and add small glowing boxes near every third spike to suggest cracks. For the belly scutes, I'm working out how to cast rays from below or in front to capture the underside surface along the rising part of the coil.

Each scute will be a flattened box oriented using the stick's local axes, with the direction computed from the center path, and I'll keep widths fixed and decreasing along the tail rather than complicating things with scaling logic. Now moving on to designing the gorget.

I'm adding glowing cracks between chest rows and scattering hexagonal shoulder plates using a filtered surface scatter. I'm also considering whether loft geometry supports sector coloring for the belly and dorsal stripes, weighing the risk that it might not be supported.

Now I'm defining non-overlapping color sectors for the top ridge, flanks, and belly, then thinking about adding a half-sunk torus ring near the rear to suggest a coiled shape, checking whether its radius fits within the bounding box.

Still, the torus exceeds the box bounds, so instead I'm sweeping loop rings around the trunk using tangent directions sampled along the path at several t-values -- thin ink seams at a few spots and thicker bone-shaded bands at others -- to read as coil segments.

For the ray cast from above, I need to guard against a null result if it misses the surface, and I'll finish off with a spiked stick in bone color topped with a small boneShade cylinder base.

I'm planning a head builder function that handles the head joint, jaw joint, mount position, scale, and direction, working out the specific joint positions and orientations for the head and jaw so they connect properly at the mount points.

Rather than relying on bone-aligned local conventions, I'm defining my own coordinate basis from the direction vector: computing forward, left, and up axes via cross products, then expressing head points in these head-local coordinates (left, up, forward) so I can place parts deterministically regardless of joint conventions. I'm also checking scale factors and bounding box limits to make sure heads stay within reasonable size constraints.

For building the actual geometry, I'm converting the basis vectors into a rotation matrix/quaternion so boxes and lofted shapes can be placed and oriented correctly in that local frame, with a helper function that handles position, color, and optional extra rotation. I'm planning the skull shape as a lofted form running from the back of the head to the snout, interpolating width and height along the way, and using mirrored x-coordinates for symmetric details.

I'm now working out how to place teeth as cones along the jaw, flipping their orientation so upper teeth point down and lower teeth point up, plus adding snout plates and brow ridges as tilted boxes.

For the eyes I'm layering a glowing sphere inside a darker socket sphere with a small bright core, and for the horns I'm sweeping a bezier curve backward from the base to shape them with bone material.

For the horn tips, I'm using a color function along the sweep that shifts toward ink near the end rather than adding separate spike geometry. The cheeks get simple boxes placed at the hinge sides, and the lower jaw hangs off the jaw joint — even though its position sits oddly forward of the mount in model space, the geometry will just follow that bone regardless. I'm setting up the jaw-open pose by rotating the jaw joint around its hinge axis.

Rotating the jaw this way at the end would pivot too far forward and look wrong, so instead I'll pre-bake the open-mouth position directly into the jaw geometry by manually rotating its local coordinates around the hinge point before building it, using a small helper to transform each point by the hinge angle.

For the mouth interior, I'm planning a dark gum box sitting atop the lower jaw, a flat lolling tongue tilted downward for the central head, teeth as small cones along the jaw edges, and a glow box tucked at the back of the throat between the jaws.

For the frill, I'm placing three bone spikes radiating outward-back from the hinge on each side, with thin triangular membrane slabs connecting the spine tips to form the fan shape. I also want small nostril boxes near the snout tip, a crown of three small horns on top of the central head, and a snout-end cap for finishing detail.

Now I'm counting total parts to stay under budget—trimming teeth to four per side instead of five brings things down to roughly 230 parts total across skull, cheeks, brow, eyes, horns, nostrils, jaw, glow throat, tongue, and frill elements. I'm also sketching out the head mounting specs, defining direction vectors for the central and four side heads (inner-left, inner-right, outer-left, outer-right), each with a slight upward tilt so the snouts angle correctly from their mount points.

Setting up local coordinate helpers that scale everything by a uniform factor, then writing a placement function that combines a basis quaternion (from local axes) with rotation offsets to position each geometry piece on its bone.
